ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, point $D$ is on side $AB$, $E$ is the midpoint of side $AC$, $CF\parallel AB$, and the extension lines of $CF$ and $DE$ intersect at point $F$. If $AB=4$ and $CF=3$, what is the length of $BD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $CF\parallel AB$,\\
it follows that $\angle ADF=\angle CFD$ and $\angle DAC=\angle ACF$,\\
since $E$ is the midpoint of side $AC$,\\
it follows that $AE=EC$,\\
in $\triangle ADE$ and $\triangle CFE$,\\
we have $\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle ADF=\angle CFD \\
\angle DAC=\angle ACF \\
AE=EC
\end{array}\right.$,\\
therefore, $\triangle ADE\cong \triangle CFE$,\\
therefore, $AD=CF=3$,\\
therefore, $BD=AB−AD= \boxed{1}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, point $D$ is on side $AB$, $E$ is the midpoint of side $AC$, $CF\parallel AB$, and the extension lines of $CF$ and $DE$ intersect at point $F$. If $AB=4$ and $CF=3$, what is the length of $BD$?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Since $CF\parallel AB$,\\ it follows that $\angle ADF=\angle CFD$ and $\angle DAC=\angle ACF$,\\ since $E$ is the midpoint of side $AC$,\\ it follows that $AE=EC$,\\ in $\triangle ADE$ and $\triangle CFE$,\\ we have $\left\{\begin{array}{l} \angle ADF=\angle CFD \\ \angle DAC=\angle ACF \\ AE=EC \end{array}\right.$,\\ therefore, $\triangle ADE\cong \triangle CFE$,\\ therefore, $AD=CF=3$,\\ therefore, $BD=AB−AD= \boxed{1}$
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right; point D is located on side AB; point E is located on side AC; after line DE is extended, it intersects the line segment CF starting from C at point F; in the figure CF is parallel to the direction of AB. Reasoning: From the meaning of the problem, E is the midpoint of AC, so AE = EC; and AB = 4, CF = 3. Compare triangles ADE and CFE: because A, E, C are collinear, and D, E, F are collinear, ∠AED = ∠CEF; also because AD is on AB, and CF ∥ AB, so AD ∥ CF, thus ∠DAE = ∠ECF. Together with AE = EC, therefore △ADE ≅ △CFE (ASA). So the corresponding side AD = CF = 3. Since D is on AB, BD = AB - AD = 4 - 3 = 1.
